_note: Living in Waynesville resource center (/resources/). Hand-kept. Facts only as each official or organization page publishes them; every entry has a source URL and the date it was verified. No private individuals' names or direct lines (department staff emails stay off). Phones are written as published. Re-verify entries older than ~90 days. Leave a field out rather than guess.

items.name: Emergency: police, fire, medical
items.what: For any emergency, including an uncontrolled fire.

items.name: Non-emergency dispatch (Warren County)
items.what: Police or fire help that isn't an emergency. This is also the Village of Waynesville's after-hours number for utility emergencies.

items.name: Waynesville Police Department
items.what: Questions, police and accident reports, vacation house checks, solicitor's permits.

items.name: Wayne Township Fire Department
items.what: Fire and EMS for Wayne Township, the villages of Waynesville and Corwin, and the Oregonia area of Washington Township. Burn permits, fire inspections, safety education.

items.name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
items.what: Free, confidential support 24 hours a day. Call or text 988.

items.name: Weather alerts and road conditions
items.what: National Weather Service forecast and alerts for Waynesville, and OHGO for state-route traffic and closures.

sections.title: Village of Waynesville
sections.intro: For homes and businesses inside village limits.

items.name: Village office (Waynesville Government Center)
items.what: General questions, utility billing, zoning, income tax, council. Office hours Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–noon and 1–4 p.m.

items.name: Water, sewer and trash bills
items.what: Pay online through Invoice Cloud ($2.95 fee), at the night drop box in front of 1400 Lytle Road, in person at the Government Center or the Waynesville branch of LCNB, or by mail to Waynesville Utility Department, 1400 Lytle Road, Waynesville, OH 45068.

items.name: Trash, recycling and yard waste
items.what: Rumpke, billed with village utilities. Pickup for all services is Monday; set items out Sunday evening.

items.name: Sewer questions (not billing)
items.what: Sewer service is billed by the village on behalf of the Warren County Water and Sewer Department.

items.name: Leaf pickup
items.what: Fall leaf pickup started Oct. 19, 2026, on a street-by-street schedule. Rake leaves to the curb, not into the street, so they don't clog storm drains.

items.name: Streets and snow
items.what: The Streets and Maintenance department plows, salts and repairs village roads and keeps up signs and signals. Call the village office with street problems.

items.name: Drinking water quality report
items.what: The village's 2025 Consumer Confidence Report, plus earlier years.

items.name: Village Council and meetings
items.what: Meeting dates, agendas and minutes.

items.name: Waynesville Food Pantry and Wayne Township Community Aid
items.what: Free non-perishable food and some paper, personal and household products, plus Community Aid help with utility bills, for residents of Waynesville, Wayne Township, Corwin, Harveysburg, Lytle and Oregonia. Distribution Monday, Wednesday and Friday, 3–4:30 p.m. Call to ask for help with food or a utility bill. To donate food, drop off non-expired, non-perishable items at the pantry during open hours, at the Mary L. Cook Library, or in the lobby of the Wayne Township Fire Station (open 24/7). The pantry doesn’t take clothing or furniture.
items.address: St. Mary’s Episcopal Church, 107 S. Third St., Waynesville

items.name: Elderly Services Program (Warren County Community Services)
items.what: Help for Warren County residents 60 and older who need help with daily tasks such as bathing, cooking or transportation and aren’t covered by another payer such as Medicaid, Medicare, insurance or hospice. A care manager visits to build a care plan. Services can include home care, home-delivered meals, medical transportation, emergency pendants, minor home repairs such as ramps and grab bars, and adult day programs. Some seniors pay nothing; others pay part on a sliding scale. To apply, call the intake line.

items.name: Warren County Community Services: senior programs
items.what: Senior nutrition, senior transportation, senior housing and other supportive services.
